problem.title: Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets)
problem.prompt: Design a Google Docs / Notion-style collaborative editor supporting 10M DAU, 100 concurrent editors per document, <80ms keystroke propagation, and seamless offline editing with automatic conflict-free merge on reconnect.

spark.summary: Building an offline-capable collaborative editor requires replacing central Operational Transformation (OT) locks with sequence CRDTs (RGA / Yjs) over sticky-routed WebSocket gateways, backed by an append-only operation log and periodic snapshot compaction.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, sequence CRDTs guarantee strong eventual consistency without a central serialization server, but require tombstone compaction and delta-state encoding so document memory does not grow unboundedly.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Concurrent offline edits break naive index-based updates (`insert(pos=5, 'x')`). **Sequence CRDTs** (such as RGA or Yjs) assign each character a globally unique, causally ordered ID `(lamport_ts, client_id)` so concurrent inserts merge **commutatively** in any delivery order.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts `Client A (Offline Edit)` and `Client B (Concurrent Edit)` each maintaining a local `RGA / Yjs Character Tree` (`a1@A`, `b1@B`), exchanging deltas through a `WebSocket Pub/Sub Gateway` with `Commutative Merge (Zero Locks)` and persisting to a `Compacted Snapshot Store + Op Log`.

**Trade-Offs & Production:** CRDTs eliminate central OT transform-server bottlenecks and support peer-to-peer/offline merges, at the cost of tombstone metadata overhead—mitigated via run-length block encoding and background GC compaction.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Hash-route document rooms to stateful WebSocket/Redis-PubSub shards, enforce per-document max op-size limits, and compact op logs every N=1,000 edits.

learningJourney.purpose: The failure mode: compare central OT index-shifting against lock-free CRDT convergence.

explanation.foundation: Classic **OT** transforms integer offsets (`insert(5, 'a')`) on a single authoritative server per document.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, sequence CRDTs guarantee strong eventual consistency without a central serialization server, but require tombstone compaction and delta-state encoding so document memory does not grow unboundedly.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets) experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: RGA/Yjs Delta Sync + Sticky WebSocket Shards + Op-Log Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: route document rooms via consistent hashing and compact tombstones asynchronously.

explanation.foundation: Think of **RGA/Yjs Delta Sync + Sticky WebSocket Shards + Op-Log Compaction** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets): The mechanism: route document rooms via consistent hashing and compact tombstones asynchronously.
explanation.core: Consistent-hash `doc_id` to a **WebSocket Room Shard** (with Redis Pub/Sub cross-pod fanout for failover). Clients exchange **state vectors** (`{clientId: maxClock}`) on reconnect to fetch only missing binary deltas, while a background compactor merges the append-only op log into a single **base snapshot** and garbage-collects deleted tombstones once all active replicas acknowledge the epoch.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, rga/yjs delta sync + sticky websocket shards + op-log compaction becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Building an offline-capable collaborative editor requires replacing central Operational Transformation (OT) locks with sequence CRDTs (RGA / Yjs) over sticky-routed WebSocket gateways, backed by an append-only operation log and periodic snapshot compaction.

learningJourney.title: Taming Tombstone Bloat & Ephemeral Cursor Presence
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: keep deleted characters and live cursors from bloating persistent state.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Taming Tombstone Bloat & Ephemeral Cursor Presence** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets): Operational control: keep deleted characters and live cursors from bloating persistent state.
explanation.core: Never persist live cursor/selection coordinates in the CRDT op log—broadcast **awareness/presence** as ephemeral volatile messages over WebSockets with a 30s TTL. For deleted text, compress consecutive deletions into run-length **tombstone ranges** and run periodic snapshot compaction.

learningJourney.purpose: Applied problems: enforce access control on reconnect and keep per-user undo local.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Permissions Revocation, Undo/Redo & Large Document Splitting** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor (CRDTs & WebSockets): Applied problems: enforce access control on reconnect and keep per-user undo local.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do sequence CRDTs (RGA / Yjs) anchor character insertions to neighbor IDs like (lamport_ts, client_id) instead of integer array indexes?

options.text: Immutable neighbor IDs make concurrent inserts commutative and idempotent regardless of delivery order or offline duration
options.feedback: Correct: integer indexes shift under concurrent edits, whereas unique causal IDs always resolve to the same total order across all replicas.

options.text: Because JavaScript arrays cannot store more than 1,000 characters
options.feedback: Incorrect: the issue is concurrent index invalidation, not array size.

options.text: To force every keystroke through a two-phase commit
options.feedback: Incorrect: CRDTs avoid synchronous 2PC locks completely.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if a CRDT-backed editor never compacts deleted characters (tombstones)?

options.text: Document metadata and cold-load latency grow monotonically with total historical edits, even if the visible text stays short
options.feedback: Correct: tombstones remain in the causal tree until compacted into a fresh base snapshot.

options.text: Deleted characters reappear randomly for other users
options.feedback: Incorrect: tombstones preserve correctness, they just consume memory and load time.

options.text: WebSockets automatically switch to HTTP/1.0 polling
options.feedback: Incorrect: tombstone bloat affects memory/storage, not transport negotiation.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should live collaborator cursor positions be stored?

options.text: In an ephemeral in-memory presence/awareness channel (not persisted in the durable CRDT op log)
options.feedback: Correct: cursor moves happen dozens of times per second and have zero durability value after disconnect.

options.text: In the durable SQLite/Postgres op log so every cursor move can be replayed
options.feedback: Incorrect: persisting ephemeral cursor moves would explode op-log storage and compaction overhead.
Incorrect: DNS is not a real-time presence channel.

prerequisites.title: CRDTs & Conflict-Free Replicated Data
prerequisites.summary: CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) are replicated data structures whose concurrent updates commute or form a mathematical join-semilattice, guaranteeing every replica converges to the exact same state without coordination or consensus.

prerequisites.title: WebSocket Real-Time Scaling
prerequisites.summary: WebSockets (RFC 6455) upgrade an HTTP connection into a persistent, full-duplex TCP frame stream; scaling to millions of concurrent connections shifts the bottleneck from request/sec to stateful memory, ephemeral ports, pub/sub fan-out, and reconnect storms.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
prerequisites.summary: Consistent hashing assigns data keys to servers in a way that limits how many keys move when servers are added or removed. This helps avoid widespread cache misses and sudden load on databases.

_nextProblem.prompt: Your payment gateway SLA requires p99.9 latency below 120 ms at 5,000 RPS. A closed-loop benchmark with 100 worker threads reports p99.9 = 45 ms, yet production alerts fire on 2.4-second timeouts during 800 ms JVM safepoint pauses. Design and implement an open-loop load harness with Coordinated Omission correction that accurately captures queueing delay during server stalls.
